info.title: ZippyGo Platform API
info.description: HTTP API of the ZippyGo platform: ordering, dispatch, fleet and commerce for on-demand delivery.

get.summary:
The public keys access tokens are signed with (RFC 7517), for local verification by the
apps and future services.
Liveness probe: the process is up and serving requests. Does not touch dependencies.

The catalogue entry for a problem code: its title, status, whether retrying can help, a
description and the field-level codes it may carry. Every problem's `type` resolves here.

Readiness probe: every store is reachable. Returns 503 with the same body otherwise, so load
balancers stop routing traffic here until the dependency recovers.

403.description: Not platform staff, `access_denied` without the owning capability's permission, or a Partner purpose on the platform route

409.description: No capability grants the purpose yet

503.description: The destination is not configured here

get.summary: The catalogue of purposes with the rules of each.

One asset: its state, the facts the destination reported and, for a stored public asset,
its address. Platform assets are visible to every signed-in person; a Partner's to its
members and platform staff.

404.description: Unknown, or not visible to the caller

delete.summary:
Discards an asset and everything derived from it, deleting the bytes at the destination;
the row stays readable as discarded. With the permission that writes the file.

403.description: `access_denied` without the permission that writes the file

404.description: Unknown, or not visible to the caller

post.summary:
Confirms an upload: the platform asks the destination to describe the file and takes every
fact from that answer. With the permission that writes the file: the owning capability's
for a platform asset, `partner:profile:write` for a Partner's (`location:write` at the
Location for a Location's), `partner:write` for platform staff on a Partner's.

400.description: A key outside the authorised folder, `unsupported_file_type` or `file_too_large` as the destination reports it

403.description: `access_denied` without the permission that writes the file

404.description: Unknown, or not visible to the caller

409.description: The destination has not received the file (retry the same grant), the file arrived readable by anyone (ask for a new grant), or the asset is discarded (`asset_not_usable`)

post.summary:
Cuts a crop from a stored picture: a new asset deriving from the original, with the

parameters.description: The picture, or a crop of it (the crop is cut from the original again)

403.description: `access_denied` without the permission that writes the file

404.description: Unknown, or not visible to the caller

A signed link to a restricted file, good for ten minutes; the reading is recorded. Members

A sized rendition of a public picture, `thumb` (160 wide), `card` (480) or `hero` (1200),
cut from the lossless crop, as WebP where the client accepts it; answered with a redirect

403.description: A partner member without a partner named

post.summary:
Asks for a one-time code to a customer's number, by SMS or on WhatsApp (SMS behind it).
The caller pays first: the source's and the device's allowances are counted before the
number is read. The answer is the same three facts whether or not the number has an
account. A code again within a minute for the same purpose is `otp_too_soon`; past the
number's ten a day, the device's five or the source's two hundred an hour, `otp_daily_limit`,
never saying which.

202.description: A code is on its way

400.description: `validation_failed`: `invalid_mobile` or `not_a_mobile` on `/mobile`, or a malformed device

409.description: `sign_in_closed`: the number's market does not admit sign-in, or the market named is not configured

503.description: A store or the message provider is unavailable

post.summary:
Completes a registration: the profile the platform can stand behind (a given name, the
number proved, an optional email) and, optionally, a first address, written at once with a
session. The market's gate is consulted again. A number another device registered meanwhile
signs in to that account (`existing_account`), this draft dropped. A registration token
past its thirty minutes, or anything that is not one, is `registration_expired`.

200.description: Registered and signed in; with cookie delivery the refresh cookie is set

400.description: `validation_failed`: the name, the email, `date_of_birth_future`, `too_young`, `terms_not_accepted`, the address (`postal_code_invalid`, `pin_far_from_address`, `invalid_mobile`), `delivery_required`

409.description: `sign_in_closed`: the market closed to sign-in meanwhile

post.summary:
Verifies a customer's code. A registered number is signed in on the customer surface,
delivered as stated (the Storefront's refresh token in the `zg_refresh_customer` cookie,
the app's in the body); a new number receives a registration context, valid thirty
minutes, and nothing about it is stored. Every failure (an unknown, expired or used code, a
code issued for another purpose, too many attempts, a wrong code) answers the same
`otp_invalid`.

200.description: Signed in, or a registration to complete; with cookie delivery a signed-in session sets the refresh cookie

403.description: `account_blocked`: the account is blocked; the detail says how to reach support

202.description: A code is on its way to the new address

400.description: Malformed address, or the account's own

503.description: A store or the delivery provider is unavailable

delete.summary: Cancels a pending change: the old address stands and the code sent is useless.

post.summary:
Confirms the change with the code sent to the new address: it signs in from now, the old
address is told, and every other session ends while this one continues. A new address
another account holds is refused, but only once its code passed.

Requests a one-time code by email or SMS for the Partner console or the Agent app. Always
accepted for a well-formed identifier, so nothing reveals whether an account exists; the
user is created on the first verification. A second code inside a minute, more than ten a
day for one identifier or two hundred an hour from one source are refused.

202.description: A code is on its way

400.description: Malformed identifier; `audience_required` on `/audience` without one, `audience_not_allowed` for Mission Control

409.description: `sign_in_closed`: the number's country is not accepting sign-in

503.description: A store or the delivery provider is unavailable

post.summary:
Exchanges a one-time code for a session on the surface the code was asked for. Five wrong
codes lock the challenge (`too_many_attempts`); wrong codes also count in the sign-in
throttle. An unknown, used or expired challenge is `code_expired`.

200.description: Signed in; with cookie delivery the refresh token is set as a cookie

202.description: The code was right and two-step sign-in is on: send an authenticator or recovery code to `POST /v1/auth/two-step/verify`

400.description: Malformed body; `audience_required` on `/audience` and `delivery_required` on `/delivery` without them; `audience_not_allowed` on `/audience`

429.description: `too_many_attempts`, or `too_many_requests` while the sign-in throttle holds the identifier or the source

post.summary:
Sets the password of the signed-in user. Once a password is set, the current one is
required even inside a valid session (`forbidden` when missing or wrong, counted in the
sign-in throttle). A change ends every session of the user on every surface, this one
included (its cookie is cleared), and is announced to the user's email; a first password
ends the other sessions.

204.description: Password set; after a change every session has ended

403.description: `forbidden`: the user has a password and `current_password` is missing or wrong; `step_up_required`: a first password needs a fresh proof (`POST /v1/auth/step-up`)

post.summary:
Sets a new password through a link, at the console it was asked from. Every session of the
user ends; two-step sign-in still applies to the next sign-in. A refused password leaves the
link unused.

204.description: Password set; sign in with it

410.description: `link_invalid`: expired, used, replaced, or asked at the other console

post.summary:
Asks for a password link. The answer is always 202, whether or not the address signs in at
this console: when it does, a link is emailed that works once, for thirty minutes, and only
at this console, and earlier links stop working. Five asks in fifteen minutes per address
and per caller are allowed; beyond that nothing is sent and the answer is the same.

400.description: Malformed email, or `audience_not_allowed` on `/audience` (the Agent app has no password link)

post.summary:
Email and password sign-in to one surface. Every failure before the password is proven,
and a surface the account may not enter, is the same `authentication_failed`, in about the
same time; five failures in fifteen minutes for one identifier on one surface, or from one
source, lock it for the rest of the window (`too_many_requests` with `Retry-After`).

200.description: Signed in; with cookie delivery the refresh token is set as a cookie. A Mission Control session of platform staff without a second factor reaches the two-step set-up only (`two_step_setup_required`)

202.description: The password was right and two-step sign-in is on: send an authenticator or recovery code to `POST /v1/auth/two-step/verify`

400.description: Malformed body; `audience_required` on `/audience` and `delivery_required` on `/delivery` without them; `audience_not_allowed` on `/audience`

429.description: `too_many_requests`: the throttle holds the identifier or the source

post.summary:
Rotates the refresh token and issues a new access token on the family's surface,
delivered as the family was created whatever the request carries. Clients with cookie
delivery send `audience` to name the cookie; clients with body delivery send
`refresh_token`; neither is `audience_required`. The token spent by the latest rotation is
forgiven for fifteen seconds and answers the same successor; an older one revokes the whole
family. Every refusal is the same 401, and clears the cookie.

requestBody.description: The refresh token, or the surface whose cookie carries it

200.description: New tokens; with cookie delivery a new cookie

400.description: Malformed body; `audience_required` on `/audience` with neither a refresh token nor a surface

401.description: No token, an unknown or spent token, or a family that ended (signed out, revoked, past its idle or absolute limit, or a surface the user may no longer enter)

post.summary:
Mints a service token for a background job (workers, the simulator, CI) from its bootstrap
credential: audience `service`, the credential's one job, at most an hour. A service token
holds no memberships and is refused by every human surface; only the routes a job may call
accept it.

Ends the current session, or with `everywhere` every session of the user on every surface,
and clears the cookie, unconditionally: the answer is 204 whether or not the session still
existed. The session is the bearer token's, or the one the cookie (named by `audience`) or
the body's `refresh_token` belongs to, so a client whose access token expired can still end
it. A view-as (impersonation) token signs nobody out (`403`): the session is ended from
Mission Control.

204.description: Signed out (or nothing to end); the refresh cookie is cleared

403.description: A view-as (impersonation) token, which signs nobody out (`forbidden`)

post.summary:
Proves the signed-in person afresh, with exactly one of: the password, an authenticator
code, or a code from `POST /v1/auth/step-up/code`. The proof stands ten minutes, for this
session only; sensitive acts refused as `step_up_required` pass after it.

400.description: Not exactly one proof, or `code_invalid` on `/code`

403.description: `forbidden`: the password or authenticator code is wrong (it counts in the throttle)

post.summary:
Sends a one-time code proving the signed-in person to the account's own email or phone,
for `POST /v1/auth/step-up`.

202.description: A code is on its way

400.description: The account has no such address

429.description: `too_many_requests`: a code was sent less than a minute ago

503.description: A store or the delivery provider is unavailable

post.summary:
Turns two-step sign-in on with a code from the app, and returns ten recovery codes, shown
once. A Mission Control session that reached the set-up only reaches everything from now.
Turns the user's own two-step sign-in off, only after the password again.

403.description: `forbidden`: the password is wrong (it counts in the throttle)

post.summary: Replaces the recovery codes with ten new ones, only after the password again.

200.description: The new codes; the old ones no longer work

403.description: `forbidden`: the password is wrong (it counts in the throttle)

post.summary:
Starts setting up an authenticator: a new secret, as text and as an `otpauth://` link the
console shows as a QR code, issued as "ZippyGo Mission Control" or "ZippyGo Partner
console". Sign-in does not change until `POST /v1/auth/two-step/confirm` proves it.

200.description: The secret to add to the app

503.description: `two_step_unavailable`: this deployment holds no two-step key; or a store is unavailable

post.summary:
Exchanges the second step of a sign-in for the session: six digits from the authenticator
app (a code already used, or an earlier one, is refused) or a recovery code (once, with or
without its dash, in either case). Five wrong codes end the challenge; wrong codes count in
the sign-in throttle. The session goes where the sign-in asked, delivered as it stated.

401.description: `invalid_code`, or `code_expired` for a challenge that ended

429.description: `too_many_attempts`, or `too_many_requests` while the throttle holds the identifier or the source

503.description: A store is unavailable, or no two-step key is configured

get.summary: Every currency.

200.description: The currency, with its version as the `ETag`

patch.summary:

200.description: The currency after the change, with its new `ETag`

get.summary: The customer's addresses, newest first, with the selected one.

post.summary:
Adds an address: the postal part, the pin the customer confirmed, what finds the door. The
first is selected by construction, a later one when `select` says so. A pin more than two
kilometres from where the locality and PIN code lie is refused (`pin_far_from_address`).

400.description: `validation_failed`: the postal part, `postal_code_invalid`, the pin, `pin_far_from_address`, `invalid_mobile` or `not_a_mobile` for the receiver

delete.summary:
Removes one of the customer's addresses. Removing the selected one selects the most
recently added of the rest.

404.description: No such address of the customer's

patch.summary: Edits one of the customer's addresses: the fields sent, the whole re-checked with its pin.

404.description: No such address of the customer's

put.summary: Selects one of the customer's addresses: the one the storefront browses from.

404.description: No such address of the customer's

put.summary:
Writes marketing consent as a whole: every channel named (`consent_channel_missing` names
each one left out), the moment of agreement kept while any channel is on and cleared when
every one is off. Codes and order messages send whatever it says.

400.description: `validation_failed` with `consent_channel_missing` for each channel left out

delete.summary: Ends every session of one of the customer's devices, by the identifier the client named.

parameters.name: device_id
parameters.description: The device identifier the client named

204.description: Every session of the device ended

404.description: No live session of the customer's on that device

get.summary:
Where the customer browses from: the selected address's pin placed as the storefront places
any pin (with the caller's `cap`); explicitly empty without an address.

parameters.name: cap
parameters.description: The cap in metres, as for the storefront's resolution; the storefront asks with 25000

get.summary: The customer's profile, with its `ETag`.

patch.summary:
Edits the profile: the named fields sent, nothing else; consent has its own operation and
the number its own change. A changed email is unverified from now. `If-Match` guards
against a stale edit.

412.description: `precondition_failed`: the profile changed since the `If-Match` version

get.summary:
The account's sections in order, each saying whether it works today and, if not, which step
of the delivery plan brings it; with the summary that answers without a click.

The sessions holding the account, newest first, each with its device (or marked
unrecognised), where it was last used and when it ends; the one asking is `current`.

delete.summary:
Ends one of the customer's sessions; it stops at its next refresh at the latest. Signing
out every session is `POST /v1/auth/sign-out` with `everywhere`.

404.description: No such live session of the customer's

get.summary:
The newest domain events, newest first. Poll with `after` set to the newest id already seen.
Platform staff see every event; partner members see their partners' events.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Only events newer than this event id (exclusive); poll with the newest id seen

get.summary:
Agents with their status and last known position, filterable by partner and status. Platform
staff see every partner; partner members see the partners they belong to.

parameters.name: partner_id
parameters.description: Only this partner's agents; every readable partner when omitted

404.description: The partner in the query is not one the caller belongs to, answered like an unknown id

post.summary:
Accepts a batch of position reports from the simulator's service token (job `simulator`),
the only credential. Validation problems are 400, unknown agents 422.

400.description: The batch failed validation; `errors` points at each field

403.description: A service token of another job

422.description: A ping references an agent that does not exist; `errors` points at the pings

get.summary:
The words for a pin, to pre-fill an address form: never stored, by the platform or by a
shared cache. An empty answer is normal, and a provider that fails answers empty too.

Places matching what was typed into an address search, best first (nearer the pin first
when one is given): locally from a bundled table of Hyderabad's localities, by prefix.

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: The country searched (alpha-2), India by default

get.summary:
Health of the API with the running version and the server time. Unauthenticated; for plain
uptime monitoring. `degraded` when any dependency is impaired or down.

Health of the API and of each dependency: Postgres, Valkey and the event outbox. The overall
status is the worst check; the HTTP status is 200 for `ok` and `degraded`, 503 for `down`,
with the same body.

200.description: The service is ok or degraded

503.description: The service is down; the body names the failing checks

post.summary:
Accepts an invitation by its token: creates the user if needed, creates the membership with
the role at its places, and signs the person in (cookie or body as for the sign-in
operations). An existing user keeps their password and two-step settings.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: The token from the invitation email

requestBody.description: The delivery of the session's refresh token, and the details used only when the user is created or has no password

200.description: Accepted: the session and the membership

202.description: Accepted; the invitee's two-step sign-in is on, so the session waits for an authenticator or recovery code

400.description: Malformed body, `delivery_required` on `/delivery`, or a weak password (`password_weak` on `/password`)

get.summary:
Live stream of agent positions and statuses: a `snapshot` frame of every matching agent when
the stream opens, then `position` and `status` frames as they change, plus a `heartbeat`
every 15 seconds. Missed frames are not replayed; reconnect for a fresh snapshot. The access
token goes in the `Authorization` header or, for `EventSource`, in `?access_token=`.

parameters.name: partner_id
parameters.description: Only this partner's agents; every readable partner when omitted

parameters.name: access_token
parameters.description: The access token, for clients that cannot set the Authorization header (EventSource)

404.description: The partner in the query is not one the caller belongs to, answered like an unknown id

get.summary: Whether live updates are available and how a client should behave; public.

Live stream of domain events as they are published: `event` events carrying an `Event` as
JSON, plus a `heartbeat` every 15 seconds. Platform staff see every event; partner members
see their partners' events. The access token goes in the `Authorization` header or, for
`EventSource`, in `?access_token=`.

parameters.name: access_token
parameters.description: The access token, for clients that cannot set the Authorization header (EventSource)

200.description: Server-sent events: `event` frames carrying an Event as JSON, and `heartbeat` every 15 seconds

get.summary:
Opens the stream: every channel named is parsed and, when private, authorised against the
caller's facts before any frame flows. Frames: `snapshot` or `resync` per channel when the
stream opens, then `signal`, `agent.position` and `agent.status` as things change,
`heartbeat` every 15 seconds, and `close` when the platform ends the stream
(`token_expired`, `revoked`, `replaced`). The access token goes in the `Authorization`
header or, for `EventSource`, in `?access_token=`; public channels need none.

parameters.name: channels
parameters.description: Comma-separated channel names from the closed vocabulary

parameters.name: client_id
parameters.description: The client's id for this connection; a new connection with the same id replaces the old one

parameters.name: access_token
parameters.description: The access token, for clients that cannot set the Authorization header (EventSource)

200.description: Server-sent events: `snapshot` or `resync` per channel, then `signal`, `agent.position`, `agent.status`, `heartbeat` and finally `close`

400.description: No channels, too many, or a name no channel produces (`channel_unknown`, errors by position)

401.description: A private channel without a credential, or an invalid token

403.description: A channel this population may not hear, errors by position

404.description: A Location or Partner channel the caller does not belong to, answered like an unknown id

503.description: Live updates are not configured in this environment

get.summary:
The signed-in user, the surface the token is for, their account and what they hold there:
their Partner memberships on the Partner console (each with its grants per scope and
whether it opens the console), their platform membership on Mission Control, their agent
memberships on the Agent app. Under a view-as session, the one consented Partner and who
views it.

200.description: The user, the surface and what they hold there

401.description: No valid token, or a Mission Control session that ended

get.summary:
Documents on file across Partners, oldest first: Mission Control's review queue. Filter with
`review`, `kind` and `partner_id` or the full grammar; platform realm only (`partner:read`).

parameters.name: review
parameters.description: Only documents in this review state

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: A filter tree as JSON over `review`, `kind`, `partner_id` and `uploaded_at`

get.summary:
Partners in pages, newest first by default; platform realm only. Filter with the named
parameters or the full grammar in `filter`, sort with up to three declared keys and ask for
facet counts alongside the page.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Only partners whose name or legal name contains this text

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: A filter tree as JSON; see GET /v1/partners/filters

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort keys, comma separated, `-` for descending (default `-created_at`)

parameters.name: facets
parameters.description: Enumeration fields to count, comma separated (`status`, `kind`)

400.description: A parameter was refused; `errors` names each with its code

post.summary:
Creates a partner, `pending`, together with its roles and its first owner, as one
operation. From the Partner console the caller becomes the owner. Mission Control onboards a
Partner on its behalf by naming its administrator in `owner` (attached as owner when they have
an account, invited by email when they do not) and may withhold permissions
(`withheld_permissions`); that needs `partner:write` and `staff:write`, platform staff must
name an owner, and a failure anywhere, the email included, leaves no Partner behind. Platform
staff activate it with `PATCH /v1/partners/{partner_id}` once nothing blocks it. Send
`Idempotency-Key` to make a repeated creation answer the first.

400.description: Malformed body, invalid fields (`gstin_invalid`, `pan_invalid`), platform staff without an `owner`, or `unknown_permission`

403.description: An `owner` or withheld permissions from somebody who is not platform staff, or `access_denied` without `partner:write` and `staff:write`

503.description: A store or mail delivery is unavailable; nothing was created

get.summary:
The fields partners can be filtered, sorted and faceted by, so a console builds its filter
bar from the declaration.

Counts of every partner by status and kind, without fetching rows, from a copy at most 30
seconds old; platform realm only.
One partner, for its members and platform staff.

200.description: The partner, with its version as the `ETag`

404.description: Unknown, or not visible to the caller

patch.summary:
Changes the members present in the body. The profile needs `partner:profile:write`
(platform staff `partner:write`); only platform staff change `status` (`partner:approve` to
activate a pending partner, `partner:write` otherwise), with a `reason` kept in the audit
log, and the kind and the GST exemption (`partner:write`). Send `If-Match` with
the version you hold to be refused when someone else changed the partner first.

200.description: The partner after the change, with its new `ETag`

403.description: `access_denied` without the permission a member of the body needs, or `forbidden` for `status` from outside the platform realm

404.description: Unknown, or not visible to the caller

409.description: `activation_blocked` with the blockers, `illegal_transition`, `locations_open` on archiving, or `partner_archived`

412.description: `If-Match` no longer matches: someone changed the partner first

get.summary:
Every grant and revocation at the partner, newest first: who acted, on whom, which role, at
what scope; filter by `user_id` or `membership_id`. `staff:read`.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: A filter tree as JSON over user, membership, role, action and occurred_at

404.description: Unknown, or not visible to the caller

get.summary:
What activating the partner needs: its status and every blocker (nobody administering it,
the documents it must have approved), the checklist the consoles show before an attempt and

What a store is doing now, the `StoreState` schema: open, shut by the clock (listed under
"Opening later"), or taken offline (listed under "Temporarily offline").

fields.description: The typed extra fields its Locations carry.

status.description: Lifecycle; only `active` may be given to a new Location.

fields.description: Typed extra fields, from the store field catalogue.

oneOf.description: New catalogue block.

StorefrontCategory.description: A category of a Vertical, the `StorefrontCategory` schema.

icon_url.description: Its icon, a rendition relative to the API host.

StorefrontHome.description: The opening screen in one answer, the `StorefrontHome` schema.

configured.description:
Whether the zone (or the city above it) configured its rows; when `false` the
storefront draws its own default arrangement of `verticals`.

place.description:
The zone drawn and how it was reached. A remembered zone the answer differs from is
forgotten on the device.

rows.description: The rows to draw, in order: Vertical tiles and the campaign banners showing now.

verticals.description:
Every Vertical the platform offers, each flagged with whether it trades here; archived
ones are absent. Empty only when nothing resolved.

StorefrontPlace.description:
Where a visitor is placed, the `StorefrontPlace` schema: the zone the storefront draws, how
it was reached and how far the pin is from it.

cap_metres.description:
The cap the caller asked with, in metres; `null` when none was given and nearest won at
any distance.

distance_metres.description:
Metres from the pin to the zone's edge: zero inside, the distance for `nearest`, `null`
for a default or a chosen zone.

oneOf.description: The pin the answer is for, when one was given whole (half a coordinate counts as none).
The zone or default service area drawn; `null` only when `resolution` is `none`.

StorefrontVertical.description:
A Vertical as the storefront holds it, the `StorefrontVertical` schema: enough to draw it
and to open its listing without another request.

categories.description: Its categories that are switched on, in the order the operator arranged them.

image_url.description: Its image, a rendition relative to the API host.

position.description: Its place in the flat list: the zone's order, then the platform's.

trades_here.description:
Whether it trades in this zone; one that does not is shown, dimmed, and does not
navigate.

StorefrontVerticalRef.description: A Vertical named in a listing, the `StorefrontVerticalRef` schema.

trades_here.description: Whether it trades in the zone.

StorefrontZone.description: A service area as the storefront names it, the `StorefrontZone` schema.

city.description: The city it belongs to, or its own name for a city.

kind.description: What it is: a zone, or a city for a default service area.

path.description: Its place in the geography tree.

time_zone.description: Its time zone, the clock its stores' hours read in.

StorefrontZoneList.description: The zones a visitor may pick, the `StorefrontZoneList` schema.

zones.description: Every zone that serves now, by city and name.

StrandedLocation.description: A Location a division would strand, named in the refusal.

SwitchBody.description: Request body of the switch routes, the `SwitchChange` schema.

reason.description: Why, kept in the audit log; required.

Target.description: The record an entry is about: a reference, never a copy.

id.description: The record's id (a UUID or a natural key such as a country code).

kind.description: The kind of record, for example `partner`, `country` or `service_area`.

label.description: The record's display label at the time, when known.

TeamMember.description: A member of a team with their access, the `TeamMember` schema.

disabled_at.description: When it was disabled, while disabled.

display_name.description: How the member is shown here: the name set for this membership, else the user's.

grants.description: Every grant, each with its scope and the permissions held there.

partner_id.description: The partner, or the platform organisation for platform staff.

items.description: The members, oldest first, each with every grant.

TeamMemberUpdateBody.description: Request body of the member changes, the `TeamMemberUpdate` schema.

display_name.description: The name the member is shown under here, or `null` for the user's own.

access_token.description: The access token, a JWT for the `Authorization: Bearer` header.

audience.description: The surface the session is for.

expires_in.description: Seconds until the access token expires; the refresh token's lifetime is never stated.

refresh_token.description: The refresh token when the delivery is `body`; `null` when it travels in a cookie.

two_step_setup_required.description:
`true` when the session reaches the two-step set-up only: platform staff without a
second factor set one up before Mission Control opens.

Trading.description: Whether a Location trades at an instant, the `Trading` schema.

until.description: When that changes, in the Location's zone.

TradingEffect.description: What a requirement does to trading.

TwoStepChallenge.description:
The second step of a sign-in, the `TwoStepChallenge` schema: the password or code was
right, and an authenticator code (or a recovery code) is awaited.

challenge_id.description: Send this back with the code to `POST /v1/auth/two-step/verify`.

expires_at.description: When the second step stops waiting (five minutes).

methods.description: What may answer it: `authenticator` (six digits from the app) or `recovery_code`.

issuer.description: The name the app files the codes under.

otpauth_uri.description: The `otpauth://` link; render it as a QR code.

secret.description: The secret in base32, for typing into the app.

TypeField.description: A typed extra field a type declares, the `TypeField` schema.

key.description: The key, from the closed field catalogue.

required.description: Whether a record of the type must carry it.

UploadGrant.description: A grant to post one file straight to the destination, the `UploadGrant` schema.

content_type.description: The exact content type the destination accepts for this grant.

fields.description: The form fields to send, every one of them, before the file part.

file_field.description: The name of the file part, sent last.

key.description: The object key the destination will hold the file under; confirm with it.

max_bytes.description: The largest size the destination accepts for this grant, in bytes.

User.description: A person, the `User` schema: who they are, never what they may do (that is a membership).

display_name.description: The name the user is shown under, `null` until set.

email.description: Email address, normalised; `null` for phone-only users.

phone.description: Phone number in E.164; `null` for email-only users.

VehicleKind.description: A vehicle a delivery Service runs.

VehicleType.description: A vehicle type with what it carries, the `VehicleType` schema.

VerificationOutcome.description: How a verified code turned out, the `CustomerVerificationOutcome` schema.

image_asset_id.description: The image shown on its tile.

VerticalCategory.description: A category of a Vertical, the `VerticalCategory` schema.

id.description: Identity that outlives renames and reorders.

VerticalCategoryInput.description: One category as sent, the `VerticalCategoryInput` schema; the id is kept when given.

id.description: The identity to keep; a fresh one when omitted.

VerticalIdsBody.description: Request body of the Vertical set and order routes, the `VerticalIds` schema.

asset_id.description: The image asset, or `null` to clear.

VerticalKind.description: Whether a Vertical lists product sales or field services.

VerticalOffer.description: A Vertical as a service area offers it, the `VerticalOffer` schema.

inherited_from.description: The ancestor whose declaration reaches here, when inherited.

offered.description: Whether the Vertical trades here: declared here or inherited, and the Vertical active.

offered_here.description: Whether this service area declares the offer itself.

items.description: The Verticals as the area offers them, in its order.

Window.description: An open window of a day, the `Window` schema.

to.description: Closes at; `00:00` means midnight at the close of the day.

Workflow.description: The workflow of a field service.

Bearer.description: An access token issued by the sign-in operations: a JWT signed with EdDSA (Ed25519), valid for 15 minutes, verifiable with the keys at /.well-known/jwks.json.
